{
  "dataset_name": "spambase",
  "model_family": "tree",
  "schema_generator": "gpt-5.5-pro",
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "offer_action_word_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Sum of word-frequency columns that represent offer or action cues in the standard Spambase column order: remove, order, free, credit, 000, and money.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        36.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "semantic_word_group",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Consolidates several sparse promotional/action terms into one thresholdable score, letting a tree split on combined presence rather than many separate branches.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "word_freq_6 + word_freq_8 + word_freq_15 + word_freq_19 + word_freq_22 + word_freq_23"
    },
    {
      "name": "contact_route_word_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Sum of routing and contact wording columns in the standard Spambase column order: address, mail, receive, addresses, email, and direct.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        39.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "semantic_word_group",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Aggregates related contact-route cues into a compact measure that supports simple tree thresholds for recipient-contact language.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "word_freq_1 + word_freq_9 + word_freq_10 + word_freq_14 + word_freq_17 + word_freq_39"
    },
    {
      "name": "personal_addressing_word_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Combined frequency of direct personal-addressing terms in the standard Spambase column order: you and your.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        28.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "semantic_word_group",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures direct-addressing intensity as a single split variable, including nonlinear interactions with punctuation and capitalization cues.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "word_freq_18 + word_freq_20"
    },
    {
      "name": "work_thread_context_word_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Broad sum of technical, workplace, academic, and correspondence-thread word columns in the standard Spambase column order.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        210.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "semantic_word_group",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures context-rich workplace or technical language in one feature, helping trees form branches for rows dominated by thread-style wording.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "word_freq_24 + word_freq_25 + word_freq_26 + word_freq_27 + word_freq_28 + word_freq_29 + word_freq_30 + word_freq_31 + word_freq_32 + word_freq_33 + word_freq_34 + word_freq_35 + word_freq_36 + word_freq_37 + word_freq_38 + word_freq_40 + word_freq_41 + word_freq_42 + word_freq_43 + word_freq_44 + word_freq_45 + word_freq_46 + word_freq_47"
    },
    {
      "name": "offer_context_balance_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of promotional, contact-route, and personal-addressing wording to workplace, technical, academic, and thread-context wording.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        102.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "nonlinear_semantic_balance",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Creates a nonlinear contrast between solicitation-style wording and context-heavy wording, giving trees useful high-versus-low split points.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(word_freq_6 + word_freq_8 + word_freq_15 + word_freq_19 + word_freq_22 + word_freq_23 + word_freq_1 + word_freq_9 + word_freq_10 + word_freq_14 + word_freq_17 + word_freq_39 + word_freq_18 + word_freq_20) / (1.0 + word_freq_24 + word_freq_25 + word_freq_26 + word_freq_27 + word_freq_28 + word_freq_29 + word_freq_30 + word_freq_31 + word_freq_32 + word_freq_33 + word_freq_34 + word_freq_35 + word_freq_36 + word_freq_37 + word_freq_38 + word_freq_40 + word_freq_41 + word_freq_42 + word_freq_43 + word_freq_44 + word_freq_45 + word_freq_46 + word_freq_47)"
    },
    {
      "name": "punctuation_emphasis_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-scaled combined frequency of exclamation, currency, and hash characters.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        4.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "punctuation_style",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Compresses heavy-tailed emphasis punctuation into a stable numeric span with direct tree split points.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(char_freq_3 + char_freq_4 + char_freq_5)"
    },
    {
      "name": "currency_or_bang_flag",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Binary indicator for conspicuous currency or exclamation usage using unsupervised training-fold scale thresholds.",
      "value_range": [
        0,
        1
      ],
      "feature_family": "punctuation_style",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a clean boolean split for rows with visibly elevated money or exclamation styling.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where((char_freq_4 > 0.08) | (char_freq_3 > 0.30), 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "structure_to_emphasis_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of structured punctuation frequency, using semicolon, parenthesis, and bracket characters, to emphasis punctuation frequency.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        18.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "punctuation_style",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Contrasts formatting-oriented punctuation with emphasis-oriented punctuation, which trees can split on to identify different writing styles.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(char_freq_0 + char_freq_1 + char_freq_2) / (1.0 + char_freq_3 + char_freq_4 + char_freq_5)"
    },
    {
      "name": "capital_extent_bucket",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ordinal bucket for capitalization extent using total and longest capital-run length thresholds.",
      "value_range": [
        0,
        3
      ],
      "feature_family": "capitalization_style",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Turns highly skewed capitalization-run measures into interpretable buckets aligned with natural tree split behavior.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where((capital_run_length_total > 1000) | (capital_run_length_longest > 100), 3, np.where((capital_run_length_total > 200) | (capital_run_length_longest > 30), 2, np.where((capital_run_length_total > 50) | (capital_run_length_longest > 10), 1, 0)))"
    },
    {
      "name": "capital_bang_interaction",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Product of log-scaled longest capital run and log-scaled exclamation frequency.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        33.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "nonlinear_style_interaction",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Creates high values only when long capital bursts and exclamation usage occur together, giving trees a direct interaction feature.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(capital_run_length_longest) * np.log1p(char_freq_3)"
    },
    {
      "name": "commercial_intent_judgment",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Ordinal 0-4 semantic score assigned from this row's word-frequency, character-frequency, and capital-run pattern for commercial offer or solicitation tone; 0 means none and 4 means very strong.",
      "value_range": [
        0,
        4
      ],
      "feature_family": "semantic_judgment",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Adds a coarse semantic view that can group diverse commercial cues into one split variable.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "work_thread_context_judgment",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Ordinal 0-4 semantic score assigned from this row's pattern for workplace, technical, academic, or ongoing correspondence context; 0 means none and 4 means very strong.",
      "value_range": [
        0,
        4
      ],
      "feature_family": "semantic_judgment",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Adds a coarse context view for rows resembling workplace or academic threads even when no single context column is large.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
